title: Best AI apps to make MCQs from your notes
summary: Turn a PDF or lecture notes into useful MCQs. A worked sampling question shows how to catch an ambiguous stem and repair the answer choices.
body_markdown:
Start with StudyFetch if you want to turn a PDF or slide deck into a quiz. The[PDF quiz guide](https://www.studyfetch.com/section/create-ai-quizzes-from-pdf-studyfetch) describes a limited free option. Give it a short, familiar page and ask for a multiple-choice question you can mark yourself. Keep the item only if the page supports one answer and you can explain why each alternative fails. That test matters more than how quickly a tool can turn a semester's worth of notes into a quiz.


## How do I choose an MCQ generator for my PDF notes?


Look for a workflow that lets you keep the original passage beside the generated question. Before choosing an app, take a page with a table, a qualification or a diagram. These make better trial material than a page of definitions because you can tell whether the output preserved the relationship the page was teaching.


Start by reading the PDF as a student would. Is it a scan of a photocopy? Does the table continue on the next page? Is the paragraph readable only because you remember what the lecturer said? If you cannot tell which heading belongs to a column, fix the input first. Type out the relevant lines with their labels or take a clearer photograph of your own notes. Keep units, arrows and words such as “except” intact. Removing one of those can change the answer.


Decide whether the task is understanding the source or practising a distinction you already understand. For the first job,[Google's NotebookLM documentation](https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16213268?hl=en) describes turning sources into study aids including flashcards. A flashcard can be a useful intermediate step: answer the front without options, then use your own mistaken answer as the basis for a distractor. For practice from PDFs, slides, Word files or photos,[start a free account with Educato](https://www.educato.com/app/start) , which publishes this guide. Full access is paid. Inspect the first items against the original before adding more files.


### Give the generator a narrow instruction


Try this request with a passage you have checked: “Use only the paragraph headed Sampling. Write a single-best-answer question that makes me apply the distinction in that paragraph to a new example. Give the options first. Put the answer, the supporting phrase and a reason for rejecting each alternative afterwards. If the paragraph cannot settle the answer, tell me what information is missing.” Keeping the key separate gives you a chance to solve the item before reading its justification.


Read the stem with the options covered. You should be able to tell what kind of answer is being asked for, such as a method, an outcome or a reason. If you need to scan the options to discover what the question means, rewrite the final sentence. Then read the options without the key. They should all answer that same question. A list containing a method, a person and an unrelated date gives away the answer before you recall the lesson.


## How can I use AI to make MCQs from notes without memorising bad answers?


Keep draft questions apart from the ones you revise, and promote each draft only after solving it against the passage. An original example shows what this check can catch.


**Example note:** “For our student survey, a stratified sample takes a random selection from every year group. A cluster sample randomly selects whole tutorial groups and includes everyone in the chosen groups.” These sentences define the terms for this exercise. Keep the question within what they establish.


**Weak draft:** “A college selects groups of students for a survey. Which sampling method did it use?” A generator might mark cluster sampling because it saw “groups”. But the note describes groups in both methods. Until you know who was selected and whether everyone in a selected group was included, the question has no defensible key.


**Revised item:** “A college draws tutorial group names at random and surveys everyone in each selected tutorial. Which design from the note did it use?” The choices are stratified sampling and cluster sampling. Cluster sampling fits because the draw selects whole tutorials. Stratified sampling, as described in the note, would require drawing students from every year group. The word “random” alone cannot distinguish the choices. A short question with two credible options is more useful here than a longer one padded with terms the passage never introduced.


### Find out whether a distractor teaches you anything


After checking the key, change the example so the other option becomes correct. In this case, replace the draw of tutorial names with a random draw of individual students from each year group. Keep the purpose of the survey the same. If changing the sampling step changes your answer for a reason you can name, you have a useful pair of revision items. If swapping a single word simply triggers a memorised label, ask for a new setting and explain the decision again.


Apply the same method to a calculation: keep the quantities and units visible, work it on paper and see whether an incorrect option corresponds to a mistake you could actually make. A distractor based on mixing the units can help diagnose a missed conversion. A random number tells you little. If the worked solution depends on rounding, the stem must give enough information to distinguish the choices at the requested precision.


Try exchanging a question with a classmate who attended the same lecture. Ask them to underline the words that made an option correct before showing them the key. If they reach the intended answer using only a telltale phrase repeated from the stem, rewrite that option. The item will be more useful when both of you have to apply the distinction taught in class.


### What should go into my revision set?


Save the final question, the corrected key and a page or heading you can find again. Make a note of the error that made the item worth keeping. On the next attempt, cover the options and answer in your own words before uncovering them. If you recognise the phrasing but cannot supply the reason, retire that version and try a fresh example. If the source itself is unclear, take the disputed sentence to your teacher before turning it into a fact to memorise.


For help choosing a workflow across subjects, see[AI study apps for Indian students](https://www.educato.com/blog/posts/best-ai-study-apps-for-indian-students) . For the step from recognising an answer to defending it aloud, read[using study apps for MBBS revision](https://www.educato.com/blog/posts/best-ai-study-apps-for-mbbs-students) .
